entities.summary: Evgeny Aramovich Abramyan was a Soviet-Armenian physicist, Professor, Doctor of Engineering Sciences, Winner of USSR State Prize, one of the founders of several research directions in the Soviet and Russian nuclear technology. Author of more than 100 inventions and several books on applied physics, Evgeny Abramyan led research teams at the Kurchatov Institute of Atomic Energy, Budker Institute of Nuclear Physics, and the Institute of High Temperatures of USSR Academy of Sciences. In the 1960s he supervised the creation of a new research discipline – engineering physics – at the Novosibirsk State Technical University, chaired the university's major faculty.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Evgeny Abramyan's work on nuclear technology and engineering physics led to significant advancements in Soviet and Russian research, shaping a major era of scientific development. His contributions had a notable regional impact on the development of nuclear energy.
